:::{#thm-time-hierarchy}
#### More time decides more problems

The [time complexity class](#def-dtime) $\text{DTIME}(n)$
is a proper subset of $\text{DTIME}(n^{1.5})$
[@arora2009computational, section 3.1].

:::

::: {.proof}
Every problem in $\text{DTIME}(n)$ is in $\text{DTIME}(n^{1.5})$,
because $n = \asymub{n^{1.5}}$.
For the other half, let $U$ be the
[universal machine](models-of-computation.qmd#thm-universal-tm),
and build a machine $D$ that, on an input $x$ of length $n$, does the following:

1. Copy the [pair encoding](models-of-computation.qmd#def-pair-encoding) $\angb{x, x}$ onto a work tape.
2. Compute the number $t = \floor{n^{1.4}}$ in binary on another work tape. <!-- hybrid-ok: the formula names the number the step computes -->
3. Run $U$ on $\angb{x, x}$, which runs the machine that $x$ [describes](models-of-computation.qmd#def-tm-description) on input $x$,
   and subtract $1$ from $t$ after each step of $U$.
   Stop $U$ when $t$ reaches $0$.
4. If $U$ halted within those steps with [output](models-of-computation.qmd#def-turing-machine) $b \in \set{0, 1}$,
   output $1 - b$.
   Otherwise output $0$.

Steps 1 and 2 take $\asymub{n \log_2 n}$ steps:
$D$ writes $\angb{x, x}$,
counts the symbols of $x$ in binary,
then does arithmetic on numbers of $\asymub{\log_2 n}$ digits.
Step 3 runs $U$ for at most $n^{1.4}$ steps,
and each subtraction takes $\asymub{\log_2 n}$ steps,
so step 3 takes $\asymub{n^{1.4} \log_2 n}$ steps,
which is $\asymub{n^{1.5}}$ because $\log_2 n = \asymub{n^{0.1}}$. <!-- inline-ok -->
So $D$ [halts](models-of-computation.qmd#def-turing-machine) on every input,
and the problem $L$ that $D$ [decides](models-of-computation.qmd#def-tm-computes) is in $\text{DTIME}(n^{1.5})$.

Suppose $L$ is also in $\text{DTIME}(n)$.
Then some [Turing machine](models-of-computation.qmd#def-turing-machine) $M$ decides $L$,
and there are a constant $c \ge 1$ and an integer $n_0$
such that $M$ halts within $c \, n$ steps on every input of length $n \ge n_0$.
<!-- hybrid-ok: the math only names the input and its length -->
Let $x$ be an input of length $n \ge n_0$,
and let $w$ be any [description](models-of-computation.qmd#def-tm-description) of $M$.
By @thm-universal-tm,
$U$ halts with output $M(x)$ within $C \, c \, n \log_2 (c \, n)$ steps
when it runs $M_w$ on $x$,
where $C$ depends on $M$ but not on $w$ or $x$.
That bound is $\asymub{n \log_2 n}$,
so there is an $n_1 \ge n_0$ such that the bound is less than $\floor{n^{1.4}}$
for every $n \ge n_1$.
$M$ has infinitely many descriptions,
so it has a description $x$ of length at least $n_1$.
On that input, $U$ finishes within the $\floor{n^{1.4}}$ steps that $D$ allows,
with output $b = M(x)$,
so $D(x) = 1 - M(x) \ne M(x)$. <!-- inline-ok -->
But $M$ and $D$ both decide $L$, so $M(x) = D(x)$,
a contradiction.
So $L$ is not in $\text{DTIME}(n)$.

:::
